# `Q-1-19` — Array Uniqueness Violation

> An array contains duplicate items where the schema requires
> every item to be unique.

## What this means

Schemas can mark an array as requiring distinct items — no value
may appear twice. When your YAML lists the same value more than
once in such an array, this error fires.

## Why this happens

The pattern usually appears in lists of identifiers where the same
identifier appears more than once: an author listed twice in a
document's `author` field, a CSS class included redundantly in a
chunk's `classes`, or a tag duplicated in a post's `categories`.

In configurations assembled by hand from several sources (one
example pulled from documentation, another adapted from a
template), the duplicate is often unintentional.

## How to fix

Remove the duplicate. If the duplicates have slightly different
spellings or capitalizations and you want both to appear, decide
which form is canonical and unify the entries — the schema treats
them as identical only when they match exactly, so a typo can
hide the duplication.

## Related

- [`Q-1-13`](Q-1-13.qmd) — array length: a similar constraint, but on the
  number of items rather than their distinctness.
